newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China buys 150,000-200,000T soymeal for Apr--trade.
newsitem.headline: China buys 150,000-200,000T soymeal for Apr--trade.

text.p: An international grains trading firm last week sold 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes of soybean meal to China at about US$245-250 per tonne, C&F China for delivery April 1997 onwards, market sources said on Tuesday.
The deal could not be confirmed and no further details were available.
Meal and oilseeds traders said the price was on the low side and that the firm was taking a huge risk.
"Hats off to them, I wouldn't do it," said one meal trader.
If international prices went up, the firm could execute the deal, but if meal prices dropped then the firm could have problems, he noted.
Chinese buyers defaulted on numerous cargoes in October and November as international meal prices dropped below previously agreed contract prices, traders said at the time.
"There is no way they can open a letter of credit now," another source said, noting he did not know how the deal would be structured.
CBOT December soymeal closed up $4.80 at $242.20 on Monday, fuelled by rumours China was still in the market for soymeal, traders said.
